sources.entry: Cardea - SSH bastion server with access control, session recording, and optional TPM-backed key protection. EUPL-1.2 Go/Docker

summary.one_liner: Cardea is an SSH bastion server that routes client connections to backend servers based on access rules in a text file, with optional session recording and TPM-backed key protection.
keywords: control who can ssh to which server
summary.what_it_does: Clients connect with any standard SSH client and encode the backend target in the SSH username (for example user@backend@bastion or user+backend@bastion). Cardea validates the client's public key and checks access rules defined in a text file, using options such as permitconnect, permitopen, permitlisten, and from. It then connects to the backend using its own key. The rules file supports macros, pipe-separated key groups, and line continuation, so it can be reviewed and versioned. Options also control environment variables, PTY allocation, port and Unix socket forwarding, time windows, forced commands, and key validity periods. Sessions can optionally be recorded in asciinema v3 format. Host key verification uses the OpenSSH known hosts format, with a strict default policy or an opt-in trust-on-first-use mode, and supports @cert-authority entries.
use_cases: Give a team controlled SSH access to internal servers through one entry point
Restrict which users can reach which backend hosts and ports
Manage SSH access rules in version-controlled files reviewed in pull requests
Protect the bastion's private key with a TPM 2.0 module
Allow only specific forwarded ports or Unix sockets for a given key
how_to_run: Write an access rules file with permitconnect options and authorized public keys
Populate the known hosts file with backend host keys (or use @cert-authority entries)
Add the bastion's public key to the backend servers' authorized_keys
Start cardea (for example: cardea --key-strategy=tpm --tpm-parent-handle=0x81000001 for TPM mode)
stack: OpenSSH known hosts and authorized_keys formats
notable: Access rules live in a plain text file, with no database or web UI required
Backend target is chosen via the SSH username, so any standard SSH client works
Optional TPM 2.0 mode prevents extraction of the bastion's private key
Fine-grained options for time windows, forwarding, environment variables, and source IPs
Optional session recording in asciinema v3 format
caveats: TPM mode is available only on Linux and Windows
Default unknown-hosts policy is strict; TOFU mode is vulnerable to man-in-the-middle attacks on first connection
Persistent TPM SRK requires manual provisioning with tpm2-tools
Backend servers must be configured to accept the bastion key and any forwarded environment variables
